effect_estimate.comment: Primary study is qualitative and reports no primary statistical effect estimate; secondary descriptive statistics from Perez et al. (2011) on water concessions and contamination are cited to contextualize interview and policy findings.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. National biofuel mandates, entrenched elite land concentration, regulatory capture/non-enforcement by the regional environmental authority (Cauca Valley Corporation, CVC), and private Bonsucro sustainability certification reinforce large-scale sugarcane producers' control over land and water in Valle del Cauca at the expense of rural and municipal household water access. Citing secondary regional data (Perez et al. 2011), the sugarcane sector holds 64% of surface water concessions (vs. 26% for households) and 88% of groundwater concessions (vs. 2% for households) and contributes an estimated 76% of pesticide, nitrogen, and phosphorus pollution (vs. 24% municipal). Primary interviews show industry actors appealing to Bonsucro to raise allowable water-use limits and lobbying CVC to classify potable aquifer water as non-potable under Decree 1541/78 and Agreement 042/2010 to avoid contamination rules and expand irrigation, while surrounding towns suffer dry-season water shortages and displaced rural residents report difficulty accessing household water and being forced to buy water.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines Bonsucro Principle 1 legalistic land-title/tenure requirements amidst unclear customary rights and outdated cadastral records (ELIGIBILITY: tenure, property, documentation); unequal surface/groundwater concession allocation and industry lobbying to reclassify potable groundwater as non-potable under Decree 1541/78 and Agreement 042/2010 (ELIGIBILITY, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION: discretion); Asocana appealing to Bonsucro to modify water-use limits for Colombia (accommodation); multi-stakeholder standard governance excluding state actors and marginalizing communities alongside elite capture/coordination between oligarchs, sugar mills, and politicians in CVC (participation, political_coordination); and CVC non-enforcement of nominal water-use and contamination restrictions (ENFORCEMENT).

evidence_quotes.quote: The violent expulsion of peasants from the land is possible in many rural areas because land title and customary land use rights are often unclear and cadastral records are inadequate or outdated.
